projects.title: 🌟🦑Winner: SqWiTS Game - Western SheHacks Best Overall and Best Use of AI on Databricks
projects.description: Squid Game-themed phone usage punishment app. Players see their chances of survival based on a Random Forest Classifier ML model fully trained from scratch on an AWS cluster. Lose all 3 lives and face Squid Game-inspired punishments: computer vision forcing players to physically gather people into frame, an AI-generated roast song, or an automated email to a contact of choice. Created with Procreate (hand-drawn guards), React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Custom CSS animations, Websockets, Python (Pandas, pyttsx3, speech_recognition, and SMTP server), OpenCV & YOLOV5, APIs (Dropbox, Replicate, OpenAI, Replicate, Minimax), Databricks (Hive Metastore, Notebook, MLFlow, AWS Infrastructure), Spark SQL, Postman, Flask, Vercel hosting​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

projects.title: 🌟🪿Winner: Flock $tocks - Technova Best Overall and Best use of PropelAuth
projects.description: Tinder but for stocks with live debates! After login, you’ll see stocks based on your preferences and income, one at a time. 3D advisors representing viewpoints on capitalism, female empowerment, and sustainability argue about a particular stock to help users make informed investment choices. Users control which advisor speaks by toggling between them with a joystick. After you are finished, personalized investment profiles and graphic dashboards are created for the stocks you "matched" with. To build this we used React, Tailwind CSS, Python, Flask, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Whisper, Streamlit, Spline, PropelAuth, and Elegoo.

projects.title: Linguini
projects.description: Linguini was built with the T3 stack using Next.js, React, Tailwind, TypeScript, and tRPC for all the endpoints that handled gameplay, groups, leaderboards, and authentication. The word and category data came from a large WordNet hypernym dataset that was cleaned in Python and loaded into a Postgres database hosted on Neon. A daily CRON job generated a new random seed so everyone saw the same category order each day. Gameplay, login with JWTs, and group actions were all handled through custom SQL tables and tRPC API routes. The whole project was deployed on Vercel and Neon.Dm to play the game we temporarily stopped the cron job.

projects.title: Raiinet
projects.description: RAIInet is a full C++ recreation of the strategy game where two players control hidden links on an 8×8 board and interact through movement, downloads, and cell effects. The project uses an MVC architecture with both text and XWindow-based graphic displays that pull state from a central controller. Abilities are implemented using decorator patterns for links and cells, enabling features such as diagonal movement, board rotation, and teleporter cells without modifying core classes. The system also includes pixel-art rendering through jpeglib, dual point-of-view displays, a GameStats layer for efficient state transfer, and a comprehensive test suite covering a wide range of edge cases.

projects.title: 🔟MIPS Assembly Compiler Built in Scala
projects.description: Part of Waterloo's enriched version of the Foundations to Sequential Programs Course. Built a fully functional compiler in Scala for a custom language with a maximal munch scanner for tokenization, input parsing into trees, context analysis, optimizing IR, and machine code generation with garbage collection.

projects.title: 🌱HydroPal - HawkHacks Submission
projects.description: HydroPal is an interactive app designed to monitor and encourage water intake by growing a virtual plant. As users drink water, the plant grows; if they don't, it shrinks. Reaching the maximum daily plant size rewards users with Metis tokens, which can be used to unlock in-app decorations or gift points to friends. The frontend is built with React, JavaScript, and CSS, while the backend leverages Python, Flask, and YOLO for real-time water tracking. Blockchain integration is achieved through Solidity smart contracts on the Sepolia testnet, with MongoDB managing user data.

projects.title: 💂‍♂️Fraud Guardian - Scotiabank x Tangerine Hackathon Submission
projects.description: Fraud Guardian is a web application built in only 4 hours! It detects job posting scams by analyzing text from descriptions or screenshots. The frontend is built with Next.js and styled using Tailwind CSS, HTML, and SCSS. The backend leverages Python and Flask, integrating Amazon Textract for text extraction from images and the OpenAI API for scam analysis. The platform supports both English and Spanish, providing scam detection and detailed feedback across languages.

projects.title: 🐙Octoprotect - 4 Month Design Project
projects.description: OctoProtect is an anti-theft system using bluetooth accelerometers to detect and notify users when their belongings are touched via an app, push notifications, and an alert system. The frontend is crafted with React Native and Redux, while the backend is built on Golang, Gin, GORM, and secured with JWT and Bcrypt hashing. The firmware, written in C using Nordic nRF52840 and Zephyr RTOS, ensures swift response, paired with software developed in Python. The device is housed in custom 3D printed casings. Our deployment strategy involves Docker and GitLab CI/CD.

projects.title: 👀SocialEye - Hack the North Submission
projects.description: SocialEye is a smart security system integrated with social media for enhanced interactivity and accessibility. It records and stores footage securely, accessible through Discord commands. Built with a Raspberry Pi and Python, it runs on a Repl server hosting a Flask web server and Discord bot. The system processes video data, stores it in Google Cloud, and presents it through an HTML/CSS frontend, redefining home security.

projects.title: 🌟⭕️Winner: Terra Taskers - Web3Apps - Best Sustainability Hack and Best use of Circle
projects.description: Created a global social media feed and payment reward system to encourage individuals to complete environmentally friendly tasks from their weekly checklist & post them. We built it using HTML/CSS, Javascript, Flask framework, Python, deta.space (for data storage), Circle API, and we made the payout system with FLOW crypto tokens.

projects.title: 🌟🌳Winner: Upleafed - SHAD Month-Long Challenge Best Prototype
projects.description: We created a device to improve wellness and connectivity in workplaces. It comes in the form of a 3D printed tree whose leaves glow red. Employees can go on an app which includes a list of tasks such as "go on a 30 minute walk with a coworker". Once they have completed the task, they submit that they have done so and a leaf on the tree changes from red to green. Once the entire tree glows green, the entire workplace earns health-related discounts and benefits. This device was created by using Arduino, HTML/CSS/SASS, Flask, Tinkercad, and Python.

projects.title: 📈Analyzing the Efficacy of an LSTM Model in Daily Stock Predictions
projects.description: Built a Python LSTM model. Historical stock prices were used to train and test the model. To test the accuracy, the predicted values were compared with the historical prices. This was done through finding regression models of the curves of best fit, correlation coefficients, coefficients of determination, measures of central tendency, standard deviations, root mean square deviations, mean absolute percentage errors, z-scores, and outliers.

projects.title: 🌟👟Winner: TSLA - A Device that Aids Individuals with Temperature Sensory Loss Caused by Diabetic Neuropathy
projects.description: Displayed at the York Region Science and Technology Fair. This project received a certificate of distinction.The TSLA is a device that was created with an ELEGOO circuit. Its purpose is to reduce the likelihood of frostbite occurring in an individual with peripheral neuropathy. This device can be inserted into an individual’s shoe. It sends out a warning when the temperature inside of the shoe is dangerously low. The temperature of the toes is also displayed in an app and on an LCD. Diabetic individuals with peripheral neuropathy will thus be safer when they go outside in the cold weather.

projects.title: 🌟😴Winner: Improving the CPAP Machine for Sleep Apnea Patients
projects.description: Displayed at the York Region Science and Technology Fair. A silver medal was rewarded for this project.My research and data collection were focused on how effective the CPAP machine is and why so many individuals with sleep apnea do not use this treatment. First, I observed the sleep patterns of sleep apnea patients. I then conducted interviews to figure out what the main concerns are about the CPAP machine. Based on my results, I constructed a model which is as beneficial as the original machine but also addresses many of the concerns which make this machine have such low social acceptance. The new design for the CPAP includes thin rubber tubing that wraps around the face and a small straw-like structure that leads into the nose. This machine is easy to remove, easy to adjust, the tubing is longer (thus allowing the patient to place the machine further away), there is less skin irritation due to minimal contact with the face, prevents claustrophobia, prevents eye irritation, and prevents mask leaks (since the mask is replaced by tubing).
